topic:
Honest fuzzy-RD inference when the compliance jump and its unknown location vanish together PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The presolve derives the known-cutoff honest-length order min(1,n^(-s/(2s+1))/kappa) and constructs legal smooth latent monotone causal mixtures over disjoint cutoff locations. Exact full-joint likelihood calculations yield a nonshrinking unknown-cutoff lower bound when n*kappa^(2+1/s)=o(log(1/kappa)), including sequences on which known-cutoff intervals shrink. A second construction assigns all response types the same smoothly varying potential-outcome table, making outcomes conditionally identical across alternatives: outcome-assisted localization cannot remove the worst-case barrier. A four-sample coarse scan, flank regression, local cutoff classifier, and fixed-center moment inversion provide a detailed strong-signal upper-bound architecture. The closest fixed-jump, known-cutoff weak-IV, and derivative-location sources were checked; no same-object collision was found in the bounded search. These results do not prove the full frontier.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Derive and explicitly evaluate the matched fixed-alpha connected-interval length inside n*kappa^(2+1/s) comparable to log(1/kappa), using sharp compensation profiles, truncated location mixtures, and effect-label testing; finish the strong-upper constants and maximal inequality.
EARLY KILL TEST: Solve the s=1 common-outcome plateau experiment through its critical window and compare the compensation profile with a finite-grid latent Lipschitz optimization. Do not replace the full kernel with separated regimes or coverage-only inversion.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the minimax fixed-alpha expected length of connected honest confidence intervals for fuzzy-RD LATE over Hölder-s regression classes when both the cutoff is unknown and the compliance jump kappa_n vanishes, including the critical window n*kappa_n^(2+1/s) comparable to log(1/kappa_n).

open_problems.why_unsolved: The literature separates the two nonregularities: Noack-Rothe handle a vanishing fuzzy first stage at a known cutoff, while Porter-Yu, Müller-Song, and Tuvaandorj study an unknown discontinuity location under predominantly sharp or directly observed jump signals. The prior transported-LATE construction supplies weak-score inversion only for fixed geometry, whereas the boundary-discontinuity construction proves a logarithmic packing cost for a linear spatial target. Combining them requires replacing independent boundary bumps by smooth monotone compliance profiles and compensating outcome profiles over many translated cutoffs, controlling their full joint likelihood while preserving separated effect labels. The resulting nonconvex union of location experiments must then be evaluated at fixed alpha, rather than reduced to a point-estimation localization rate.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A lower-and-upper minimax theorem giving the connected confidence-interval expected-length frontier, including its sharp fixed-alpha critical-window value when obtainable, as an explicit function of n, kappa_n, s, and log(1/kappa_n), with least-favorable compensation profiles and regime statements covering nonshrinking, critical, and oracle-known-cutoff behavior.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves from fuzzy-RD ratio inference through weak-first-stage failure to honest Anderson-Rubin inference; cutoff uncertainty is the natural additional nonregularity.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Fuzzy RD identifies LATE by a ratio -> a small first-stage jump invalidates ordinary ratio inference -> bias-aware inversion restores honesty at a known cutoff -> a cutoff becoming unlocalizable with the same shrinking jump creates a new length frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Use ordered moduli and least-favorable pairs to convert uniform coverage into fixed-alpha expected-length lower bounds and construct bias-aware intervals attaining the benchmark.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target is an honest-length decision problem over smooth classes, but its modulus must be enlarged to a union of translated cutoffs with a vanishing denominator.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert bias-aware local-polynomial tests of the transformed reduced-form moment Y-theta D using exact worst-case smoothness bias bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly supplies the fixed-cutoff weak-denominator component that the joint cutoff-effect experiment must retain.

method_exemplars.technique: Rescale the local cutoff contrast under a contiguous shrinking jump and prove convergence to two-sided Brownian motion with triangular drift.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest limiting-process calculation for a smooth regression with an unknown vanishing jump; the new experiment adds location entropy, compensation, and effect labels.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a computationally explicit same-sample confidence interval for fuzzy-RD LATE that is uniformly honest over unknown cutoffs and vanishing first stages, yet recovers the oracle known-cutoff length above an explicit localization boundary.

open_problems.why_unsolved: A plausible construction scans treatment uptake, refines the cutoff locally, and inverts a weak-identification-robust moment at the selected center. However, multiscale change-point likelihood control assumes a step-like signal rather than an unknown smooth RD baseline, so candidate-cutoff scores need sharp bias-compensation envelopes. The same treatment observations also choose the cutoff and form the weak denominator, making the selector non-ancillary; local-polynomial weights, bandwidth, center, and tested effect label are jointly selected. Existing break-selection and empirical-process results do not combine this dependence with Hölder bias and a vanishing causal denominator, while the prior selected-event and sharp-RD proposals explicitly leave selection honesty and fuzzy-Wald coupling unresolved.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An implementable scan-refine-invert procedure with a uniform coverage theorem, a maximal inequality controlling all candidate cutoff-effect pairs, and an oracle-efficiency theorem showing that its connected interval matches known-cutoff bias-aware length above a stated signal threshold.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames the practical unknown-cutoff problem as detection, cutoff estimation, and effect estimation, which matches the constructive upper-bound narrative.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: RD inference normally presumes a disclosed cutoff -> some assignment thresholds are hidden or behaviorally determined -> the cutoff must be detected before estimating an effect -> weak compliance makes cutoff selection and honest effect inference inseparable

method_exemplars.technique: Aggregate scale-calibrated local likelihood tests into a multiscale scan with simultaneous error control and confidence sets for change locations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The cutoff is an unknown change location with a vanishing signal, but smooth-baseline RD contrasts must replace the source paper's step-model likelihoods.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert null-indexed local-polynomial moments with worst-case smoothing-bias critical values, avoiding weak-denominator linearization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After localization, the procedure still requires weak-identification-robust LATE inference rather than a ratio CLT.

method_exemplars.technique: Couple a growing empirical-process supremum to a Gaussian supremum and validate multiplier critical values using anti-concentration.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Scanning jointly over cutoff, scale, and effect labels creates the maximal stochastic term absent from fixed-center RD arguments.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize exactly when the outcome process improves localization of an unknown fuzzy-RD cutoff beyond treatment uptake alone as the compliance jump vanishes, and quantify the resulting improvement in honest LATE-interval length.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Multivariate change-point methods pool aligned channels whose signal is an unrestricted vector or distributional norm. In fuzzy RD, treatment and reduced-form outcome jumps share a location and are causally coupled through LATE, while smooth potential-outcome variation can compensate for or erase the outcome jump. The lower-bound problem therefore requires optimizing joint likelihood separation over admissible causal latent mixtures rather than adding squared channel jumps; the upper-bound problem must decide when an outcome contrast is reliable without sacrificing uniform coverage. Existing Bayesian unknown-cutoff RD work addresses posterior uncertainty but not the frequentist information condition or honest-length benefit.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient information condition in terms of admissible treatment and outcome discontinuities and their covariance, together with matching lower and upper honest LATE-interval length bounds and a least-favorable common-outcome construction showing when outcomes provide no localization gain.

writing_exemplar.why: It foregrounds the substantive damage from using the wrong cutoff and treats cutoff uncertainty as part of causal-effect estimation without claiming the desired frequentist frontier.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: RD effects are local to an assignment threshold -> the operative threshold may be unknown -> outcomes and treatment uptake may both appear to locate it -> causal restrictions determine when outcome information is genuine rather than illusory

method_exemplars.technique: Use information-theoretic lower bounds for shrinking multivariate changes and a kernel localization statistic that aggregates channel evidence.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Treatment and outcome are aligned channels sharing one change location, but the destination replaces unrestricted multivariate separation by a causal feasible set.

method_exemplars.technique: Index transformed outcomes Y-theta D by candidate effects and invert uniformly bias-bounded local-polynomial jump tests.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The transform exposes how outcome and treatment information interact for a candidate LATE and can be embedded in a joint localization statistic.

open_problems.open_problem: Identify primitive local-regression, cutoff-classification, and score-moment rates that are sufficient and nearly necessary for feasible unknown-cutoff fuzzy-RD inference to attain its oracle honest-length frontier under a vanishing compliance jump.

source_refs.excerpt: Turn the rare-learning boundary handle into an explicit two-point spline perturbation
unknown propensities require control of random cell denominators and their scale estimate

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior rare-event run found that high-level score-information and nuisance-product assumptions can conceal the substantive learning boundary and explicitly requested a moving-nuisance two-point perturbation. The transported-LATE result is feasible only under regular finite-cell geometry and records random denominator and scale control as the obstruction beyond that class. Unknown-cutoff fuzzy RD introduces a further error channel because cutoff error shifts both one-sided regressions by an amount amplified by inverse compliance strength. A fixed-location cross-fit expansion cannot establish the required result: its remainder analysis must become uniform in a random center and track interactions among flank-regression error, cutoff error, bandwidth, score tails, and the shrinking jump.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sufficient-condition theorem and matching moving-nuisance local-alternative counterexample expressed in explicit rates for cutoff error, one-sided regression error, bandwidth, smoothness, score tails, and compliance strength, with a studentized limit law and honest-length attainment inside the feasible region.

writing_exemplar.why: Its weak-LATE score-inversion framing supplies the fixed-location baseline from which to expose the additional unknown-location learning boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: LATE is a ratio -> weak compliance defeats Wald inference -> orthogonal score inversion restores fixed-location validity -> estimating an unknown cutoff creates an amplified nuisance remainder

method_exemplars.technique: Use fold-conditional orthogonal-score expansions to separate empirical score noise from second-order nuisance drift.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the base feasible-score proof architecture, but every remainder must be normalized by the shrinking local first stage and made uniform over the estimated cutoff.

method_exemplars.technique: Track growing representer norms and regularization bias for increasingly irregular or local linear functionals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A shrinking-bandwidth RD contrast divided by a vanishing compliance jump has an unstable score norm analogous to a shrinking-local functional.

method_exemplars.technique: Use robust-bias-corrected local-polynomial studentization with a uniform coverage-error expansion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The flank regressions require explicit bias and scale control before their errors can be propagated through cutoff classification and weak moment inversion.

open_problems.open_problem: Quantify the expected-length cost of requiring a connected fuzzy-RD confidence interval when profiling over an unknown cutoff produces multiple weak-instrument effect branches, and characterize when the unrestricted inversion set is disconnected.

source_refs.excerpt: No claim is made for ... disconnected-set taxonomy, or sharp constants.
certified polynomial root isolation enumerating every interval and ray

open_problems.why_unsolved: The transported weak-LATE frontier explicitly leaves confidence-set topology unresolved, while the BudgetIV archive enumerates components and rays only for a finite-dimensional rational lower envelope. Profiling over a continuum of candidate RD cutoffs unions many weak-ratio acceptance sets; label switching across locations can create separated branches even when each fixed-cutoff set is simple, and taking the connected hull can bridge widely separated effect labels. The first BudgetIV proof step that fails is polynomial root isolation: the finite family of rational boundary polynomials becomes a cutoff-indexed stochastic profile whose extrema and branch mergers require uniform control.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem characterizing the number and merger conditions of cutoff-profile score-inversion components, together with upper and lower bounds for the excess minimax expected length of the shortest honest connected interval relative to the shortest unrestricted honest confidence set.

writing_exemplar.why: Its central object is the geometry of a LATE confidence set obtained by weak-score inversion, the appropriate baseline before adding cutoff profiling and connectedness.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Weak-LATE inversion can yield non-Wald sets -> set geometry records weak identification -> profiling over unknown cutoff creates additional branches -> quantify the price of reporting one connected interval

method_exemplars.technique: Classify ratio confidence-set geometry through Fieller-type quadratic inversion, including bounded, unbounded, and disconnected cases.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each candidate-cutoff fuzzy-RD effect is a ratio, so Fieller geometry supplies the local branch classification that the profile union must extend.

method_exemplars.technique: Analyze the algebraic shape and regular-limit behavior of a weak-LATE score-inversion set.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest causal-ratio topology result; the new step is tracking how components evolve and merge over cutoff location.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive fixed-alpha optimal confidence procedures and expected-length efficiency from modulus geometry.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested comparison is decision-theoretic rather than merely topological: it asks for the length cost of connectedness.

literature_map:
1. Hahn, Todd, and Van der Klaauw (2001, Econometrica) give the foundational known-cutoff fuzzy-RD Wald/LATE identification argument.
2. Porter and Yu (2015, Journal of Econometrics) estimate an unknown RD discontinuity point, but center the analysis on sharp RD and only briefly discuss fuzzy RD.
3. Feir, Lemieux, and Marmer (2016, JBES) document size distortions from weak fuzzy-RD first stages and propose null-restricted weak-ID inference.
4. Noack and Rothe (2024, Econometrica; arXiv:1906.04631) combine Anderson-Rubin inversion with explicit smoothing-bias bounds for honest weak-fuzzy-RD confidence sets at a known threshold.
5. Armstrong and Kolesár (2018, Econometrica; arXiv:1511.06028) provide optimal-CI and modulus machinery; their 2020 Quantitative Economics paper specializes simple honest intervals to nonparametric RD.
6. Low (1997, Annals of Statistics) establishes expected-length restrictions for honest nonparametric confidence intervals and limits unsupported smoothness adaptation.
7. Tuvaandorj (2020, Journal of Econometrics) maps sharp RD with an unknown threshold to a discontinuous-drift white-noise model and derives minimax cutoff-location rates.
8. Müller and Song (1997, Statistics & Probability Letters) obtain shrinking-jump localization and a triangular-drift Brownian limit for an unknown discontinuity in smooth regression.
9. Frick, Munk, and Sieling (2014, JRSSB; arXiv:1301.7212) provide multiscale honest change-point sets and detection guarantees for vanishing step signals.
10. Wang, Yu, and Rinaldo (2020, Electronic Journal of Statistics; arXiv:1810.09498) exhibit logarithmic detection and localization barriers for shrinking mean changes.
11. Andrews, Kitagawa, and McCloskey (2021, Journal of Econometrics) show why inference after estimating a break location must account for selection-induced randomness.
12. Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2014, Annals of Statistics; arXiv:1212.6885) supply Gaussian coupling and anti-concentration tools for cutoff-by-scale maxima.
13. Kowalska, van de Wiel, and van der Pas (2025 version; arXiv:2406.11585) model unknown-cutoff uncertainty jointly with RD effects but do not give a frequentist honest minimax frontier.
14. Madrid Padilla, Yu, Wang, and Rinaldo (2022, IEEE Transactions on Information Theory; arXiv:1910.13289) give multivariate nonparametric change-point bounds relevant to outcome-assisted localization.
15. The central tension is that weak-fuzzy-RD papers assume the cutoff known, while unknown-cutoff minimax papers observe a sharp jump directly; the bounded scan found no paper joining an unknown cutoff, a vanishing compliance jump, connected honest LATE-interval length, and the critical location-entropy window.
